title: Nutty Light Filipino Caramel Cake
description: A light and comforting Filipino dessert featuring caramel, toasted nuts, and a hint of pickled flavor. This dairy-free-friendly cake is perfect for snacking or special occasions.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.notes: non-dairy egg substitute, e.g. flaxseed or chia seeds

instructions: Grease two 9-inch (23cm) round cake pans and line the bottoms with parchment paper.
In a medium bowl, whisk together the almond flour, coconut sugar, baking powder, and salt.
In a large bowl, whisk together the non-dairy butter, vanilla extract, and pickled ginger juice.
Add the eggs one at a time, whisking well after each addition.
Add the unsweetened coconut milk and whisk until smooth.
Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, whisking until well combined.
Fold in the chopped toasted almonds.
Divide the batter evenly between the prepared pans and smooth the tops.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center of each cake comes out clean.
Allow the cakes to cool in the pans for 5 minutes, then transfer them to a wire rack to cool completely.
Once the cakes are completely cool, place one layer on a serving plate and spread a layer of caramel sauce on top.
Place the second cake layer on top and drizzle with the remaining caramel sauce.
To make the nuka-pickle syrup, combine 1 cup of water, 1 cup of sugar, and 1/2 cup of pickled ginger juice in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes.
Strain the syrup through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl.
Let cool to room temperature, then refrigerate until cold and syrupy.
To assemble the cake, drizzle the nuka-pickle syrup over the top of the cake and sprinkle with chopped toasted almonds.
